title: Dual Carbohydrate Recognition by the Chitinase-like Protein CHI3L1 Through Distinct Glycosaminoglycan and Chitin-Binding Interfaces
authors: Önder Kurç; Nick Rähse; Mohanraj Gopalswamy; Alexandra Großdorf; Christian Gorzelanny; Jonathan Cramer; Holger Gohlke
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CHI3L1蛋白与糖胺聚糖和几丁质寡糖的双重碳水化合物识别，虽用分子动力学模拟但对象为蛋白-糖类互作，非蛋白质-DNA体系，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: CHI3L1 (YKL-40) is a chitinase-like glycoprotein involved in immune regulation, tissue remodeling, and cancer, yet the molecular principles governing its glycan interactions remain incompletely defined. Previous reports suggested that CHI3L1 can bind to chitin oligosaccharides (COS) and glycosaminoglycan (GAG) ligands, however, the molecular basis and binding sites underlying these interactions remain controversial. Here, a combination of biophysical and computational methods is employed to shed light on carbohydrate interactions of the protein and delineate a potential crosstalk between its glycan-binding interfaces. Our results demonstrate that COS and GAGs bind to distinct, non-overlapping sites on CHI3L1. Both ligand classes exhibit a strong dependence of binding affinity on the degree of polymerization. Molecular dynamics simulations, supported by mutational analysis, identify a GAG-binding site centered on residues R144, R145, and K147 and reveal an additional distal interaction site for longer GAG ligands. Biophysical and biochemical assays fail to confirm a previously proposed allo-or orthosteric interaction between both binding sites. However, physiologically relevant protein–protein interactions mediated by the chitin binding site of CHI3L1 are differentially regulated by GAG and COS ligands. COS inhibit binding of galectin-3 to CHI3L1, whereas GAG ligands enhance the affinity between the proteins by ca. 14-fold. Together, these findings establish CHI3L1 as a dual carbohydrate-binding protein with distinct recognition interfaces and reveal a previously unrecognized role for GAGs in modulating CHI3L1-mediated signaling interactions.
abstract_zh: CHI3L1 (YKL-40) 是一种几丁质酶样糖蛋白，参与免疫调节、组织重塑和癌症，然而调控其聚糖相互作用的分子原理仍未完全明确。既往报道提示CHI3L1可结合几丁质寡糖（COS）和糖胺聚糖（GAG）配体，但这些相互作用背后的分子基础和结合位点仍存在争议。本研究结合生物物理和计算方法，以阐明该蛋白的碳水化合物相互作用，并描绘其聚糖结合界面之间潜在的交叉对话。我们的结果表明，COS和GAG结合于CHI3L1上不同且不重叠的位点。两类配体的结合亲和力均强烈依赖于聚合度。分子动力学模拟，辅以突变分析，鉴定出一个以残基R144、R145和K147为中心的GAG结合位点，并揭示了一个针对较长GAG配体的额外远端相互作用位点。生物物理和生化实验未能证实先前提出的两个结合位点之间的别构或正构相互作用。然而，由CHI3L1几丁质结合位点介导的生理相关蛋白-蛋白相互作用，受到GAG和COS配体的差异性调控。COS抑制galectin-3与CHI3L1的结合，而GAG配体则将蛋白间亲和力增强约14倍。综合来看，这些发现将CHI3L1确立为一种具有独特识别界面的双碳水化合物结合蛋白，并揭示了GAG在调节CHI3L1介导的信号相互作用中此前未被认识的作用。
